findings.location: content.body.steps[id=s4].blocks[0].text: 'У питанні та після заперечення артикль часто пропускають: ¿Tienes perro? Tengo coche.'
findings.description: The explanation mentions questions and negation, but its second example, 'Tengo coche', is affirmative. The examples therefore do not illustrate the stated distinction and leave affirmative article omission unexplained.
findings.suggestion: Explain the alternatives directly, for example: 'З деякими іменниками після tener можливі обидва варіанти: Tengo un coche / Tengo coche; ¿Tienes un perro? / ¿Tienes perro? У запереченні: No tengo coche.'

items.reviewerAnswer: The tener paradigm and the possession and physical-state examples are correct. Article omission with tener is also possible in affirmative clauses.
sources: Supplied content.body.steps[id=s4].blocks[0].text.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, discussion of bare singular nominal objects with tener (from memory).

findings.location: task.errors[id=e3]: text 'Pablo tiene pelo largo.', outcome 'unresolved', feedbackUk 'Так теж кажуть; найчастіше — з артиклем: Pablo tiene el pelo largo.'
findings.description: The articleless sentence is acceptable for the stated meaning. It has already been reviewed, and its feedback acknowledges its acceptability, yet it is placed among errors and receives no correct outcome.
findings.suggestion: Move 'Pablo tiene pelo largo.' into accepted. Retain the article-bearing sentence as the reference model if preferred.

items.reviewerAnswer: Pablo tiene el pelo largo. Also acceptable: Pablo tiene pelo largo.

findings.location: task.errors[id=e2].feedbackUk: 'Tienen — для ellos або ввічливого ustedes; друзям на «ти» — ¿Tenéis sed?'
findings.description: The intended plural address system is unspecified. The feedback fits the vosotros system, but familiar ustedes also occurs in parts of mainland Spain. Spain Spanish alone does not establish that ustedes must be formal.
findings.suggestion: Specify that this exercise requires the vosotros system. Alternatively, acknowledge familiar regional ustedes usage and assess that answer accordingly.

items.reviewerAnswer: ¿Tenéis sed? In familiar western Andalusian ustedes usage, ¿Tienen sed? can also fit.
sources: Course contract rule 8 and the verdict instruction concerning unspecified regional acceptability.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, entry 'usted', discussion of familiar plural ustedes in parts of Andalusia (from memory).
